Subject: Re: Thanks — post-call request for rerank numbers and next steps

Hi Priya — thanks for the notes and great questions. Quick readout below and a proposed A/B plan. I attached the prompt set and the CSV with the aggregated eval metrics (shopline-rerank-ndcg-mrr-20261120.csv).

Summary of sample run (50k queries, stratified by recency + traffic):
- Baseline (Shopline current ranker): NDCG@10 = 0.421, MRR = 0.287
- Redwood rerank candidate A (redwood-rerank-7b-v2, default prompts): NDCG@10 = 0.473 (+12.4%), MRR = 0.331 (+15.3%)
- Redwood rerank candidate B (rwr-3b-quant, tuned prompt set v1): NDCG@10 = 0.458 (+8.8%), MRR = 0.322 (+12.2%)

Notes and caveats:
- Statistical significance: improvements above are significant at p<0.01 on the overall holdout, but variance increases on the long-tail bucket (queries with <5 historical clicks).
- Recency-sensitive queries: candidate A shows a smaller uplift on items added in the last 7 days — likely because the model relies on content signals that lag SKU updates. We recommend adding a recency-feature to the candidate scoring or using a hybrid fallback for <7d items.
- PII/logging: our test harness masks user identifiers and we can route logs to your VPC for the Private deployment or to a redacted test stream for Hosted (detail in link).

Recommended prompt set: attached prompt-set-v1.jsonl — includes explicit instructions for conservative re-ranking and a clarify-and-verify header to reduce hallucination risks on sparse queries.

Proposed A/B rollout (canary -> ramp):
1) Canary (5% search traffic, 2 weeks) — monitor NDCG@10, MRR, CTR, and customer-facing errors.
2) Segment-based ramp (next 10%): if no regression in recency/long-tail segments, increase to 20% over 1 week.
3) Full ramp (remaining traffic) pending sign-off.

Guardrails and rollback triggers:
- Any 4% absolute drop in NDCG@10 for the recency bucket vs baseline => immediate rollback.
- User-facing error rate > 0.5% for search sessions => pause and investigate.

Action items:
- Jasmine: share full CSV + prompt set (done, attached).
- Marissa/Karthik: can you prepare the canary config and the monitoring hooks?
- Priya: confirm legal requirements for log routing (VPC or redacted stream) and availability for a short call Mon/Tue.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai

Attachments: shopline-rerank-ndcg-mrr-20261120.csv, prompt-set-v1.jsonl, ab-test-proposal-20261121.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Thanks — post-call request for rerank numbers and next steps

Thanks for the summary, Jasmine. A couple of pragmatic notes from the eval side:

- Holdout split: we used a temporal holdout (last 7 days held out) plus a randomized 10% of historical traffic for variance estimation. For the long-tail bucket, the sample size is smaller (~3k queries), so confidence intervals widen — recommend extending the canary length to 3 weeks if Shopline wants stronger power on long-tail metrics.

- Segment-level thresholds: instead of a single absolute NDCG drop trigger, propose per-segment relative thresholds (e.g., allow up to 1% fluctuation on head queries but tighten to 0.5% on recency-sensitive items). This avoids noisy rollbacks from high-volume segments.

- Baseline tuning: if Shopline can provide a small click signal export for the dated SKUs, we can tune the candidate A prompt to better surface very recent items without retraining. That would likely close the recency gap we observed.

I'll start drafting the canary monitoring dashboard (per-route NDCG, MRR, CTR, latency, errors) and share the Grafana link by Monday.

-Marissa
Product Lead, Eval & Evals Infrastructure
